content:
Rep. Randy Fine (R-Fla.) went after Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) on Wednesday by suggesting that the progressive Democrat’s past experience as a bartender doesn’t stack up to his own “successful” background.

“Look, if Americans want to elect a former bartender as their president, then that’s up to them,” said Fine when asked about Ocasio-Cortez launching a possible 2028 presidential bid on Newsmax.

“But I think we need people who have had to be successful in the real world, who have gone out and done things and understand how you start, build and grow a family. How you start, build and grow a business — how you succeed in the world, because the fact of the matter is, being successful in government does not mean that you’re successful in life.”

Fine, a former casino industry executive who has been backed by President Donald Trump over the years, went on to stress that he steered clear of a political career until he spent 20 years raising his family and started multiple businesses.

“I think people like AOC and so many of these community organizers and lifetime Ph.D. candidates, they just don’t know anything, and so their policies don’t work as a result,” he concluded.

Fine’s working-class dig has been served up by right-wingers in the past, including former Trump Justice Department adviser Alina Habba, who once called the congresswoman’s intellect into question due to her job behind a bar.

AOC used Habba’s jab at the time to emphasize Trump and friends’ “disdain” for the working class and, in comments on the House floor last summer, looked back on her bartending experience to put on for service workers while arguing against the president’s so-called “Big Beautiful Bill.”

The MAGA lawmaker’s comments were swiftly met with criticism on X including by Oliver Hidalgo-Wohlleben, the congresswoman’s former campaign manager and senior adviser.

“Even after a blowout loss, Republicans can’t hide their disdain for working people,” wrote Hidalgo-Wohlleben, referring to the blue tsunami seen as a referendum on the president’s second term.

Progressive commentator @onehandpolitics, a.k.a. Mason, also weighed in, noting that Ocasio-Cortez worked the job to help support her family financially to save their home from foreclosure.

“Republicans elected a billionaire who inherited his wealth, but think a woman who worked for hers doesn’t understand the real world,” he added.

“Their contempt for the working class is despicable.”

And another user wondered aloud why Republicans like Fine have used Ocasio-Cortez’s bartending past as a jab in the first place, noting that it’s “such a common job for all types of people throughout every phase of life.”

“Doing this out of one side of your mouth while pretending to be for working people out the other is counterintuitive,” the user wrote.
